Engineering Progress Documentation

Edge-AI Based
Mine Safety & Rescue UGV

Prototype status, system architecture, sensor integration, Wi-Fi telemetry and LoRa communication development
Document ID: UGV-PDR-001 Revision: 1.2 Prepared: November 2026 Stage: Prototype integration

1. Executive Summary

The Edge-AI Based Mine Safety & Rescue Unmanned Ground Vehicle (UGV) is a mobile robotic platform for remote inspection and environmental monitoring in locations that are difficult or risky for people to inspect directly.

The prototype is built on a four-wheel chassis with ESP32-based electronics. Its environmental sensing subsystem combines an AM2301 (DHT21) temperature and humidity sensor with MQ-2 and MQ-135 gas-response modules. Two ultrasonic sensors measure nearby obstacle distance, and an ESP32-CAM provides live visual monitoring. All sensors and the camera operate together over Wi-Fi, which is the working communication link of the prototype. A LoRa SX1278 link is under development as a long-range telemetry channel.

2. Introduction and Motivation

Underground mines present restricted visibility, confined passages, debris, water accumulation and potentially hazardous atmospheric conditions. After an incident, an initial inspection can expose rescue personnel to unknown risks.

A remotely operated UGV acts as an inspection platform: it carries sensors and a camera into the area while the operator stays at a safer location.

2.1 Project concept

  • Mobile robotic platform for remote inspection and monitoring.
  • Environmental sensing with low-cost sensor modules.
  • Short-range obstacle-distance estimation with ultrasonic sensors.
  • Wi-Fi sensor telemetry and live camera feed.
  • LoRa link for long-range telemetry (in development).
  • Edge-AI, mapping and autonomous navigation as later stages.

4. System Architecture

The system is organised into mobility and motor control, environmental sensing, obstacle-distance sensing, visual monitoring and wireless communication. ESP32 boards acquire sensor data and provide the Wi-Fi interface; LoRa is being developed as a second communication path.

Obstacle sensingUltrasonic trigger/echoDistance to nearby objects.
Visual monitoringESP32-CAM image sensorCamera feed over Wi-Fi.

4.3 Evolution from the reference design

The initial Trinetra reference architecture used three ESP32 controllers (motors and encoders; sensing with onboard LoRa; stationary LoRa station) and L298N drivers. The prototype has evolved to two ESP32 DevKit V1 boards, two BTS7960 motor drivers, an integrated ESP32-CAM and Wi-Fi as the working link, with the SX1278 LoRa link now in development.

5. Mechanical and Mobility Platform

The prototype uses a four-wheel chassis that carries the electronics and sensing modules. The drive system uses four 12 V geared DC motors with encoder connections on the motor assemblies.

5.1 Drive arrangement

Two BTS7960 motor-driver modules drive the vehicle: one for the left-side motor pair and one for the right-side pair. This provides differential (skid) steering for forward, reverse and turning motion.

6. Electrical Power Architecture

A 12 V battery supplies the vehicle through a fuse and main switch. An LM2596 buck converter provides the regulated low-voltage supply for the electronics.

Battery positive → fuse → main switch → switched 12 V distribution.
The switched supply feeds the motor-driver power inputs and the buck-converter input. Battery negative, motor-driver ground, buck-converter ground and controller/sensor grounds share a common reference.

6.1 Design rules followed

  • Motors and other high-current loads are never powered from ESP32 GPIO pins or breadboard tracks.
  • Buck-converter output is measured with a multimeter before electronics are connected.
  • Battery and motor-current paths use appropriately sized wire and secured terminals.
  • Motor-current wiring is kept separate from low-level analogue sensor wiring.

7. Embedded Controllers and Communication

7.1 ESP32 controllers

Two ESP32 DevKit V1 boards perform sensor acquisition and wireless communication. The ESP32-CAM runs the camera and its own Wi-Fi stream.

7.2 Wi-Fi telemetry — working

Wi-Fi is the working communication method of the prototype. Sensor values are acquired at the vehicle, formatted into data records and transmitted over the local Wi-Fi link, while the ESP32-CAM supplies the live camera feed through its own Wi-Fi connection. The temperature, humidity, gas-sensor and ultrasonic readings run together with the camera.

7.3 LoRa SX1278 communication — in progress

An SX1278-based LoRa link is being developed using Ai-Thinker RA-02 modules in the 433 MHz band, as a point-to-point link between a vehicle-side transmitter and a stationary receiver. The reference radio configuration is spreading factor 9, bandwidth 125 kHz and one telemetry packet per second.

LoRa is a low-data-rate channel, so it is used for compact sensor telemetry and status. The camera feed stays on Wi-Fi.

7.4 LoRa development sequence

  1. Wire the SX1278 to the ESP32 over SPI (SCK, MISO, MOSI, NSS, RESET, DIO) on a stable 3.3 V supply with common ground.
  2. Run radio initialisation on both modules.
  3. Send numbered test packets from transmitter to receiver on matching radio settings.
  4. Run a sustained packet test counting sent, received and missed packets.
  5. Test range and antenna orientation.
  6. Integrate the compact sensor payload into the LoRa packet.

8. Environmental Monitoring Subsystem

8.1 AM2301 (DHT21) temperature and humidity sensor

The AM2301 measures ambient temperature and relative humidity over a single-wire digital interface on ESP32 GPIO 4, and produces stable readings.

8.2 MQ-2 module

The MQ-2 module is powered from 5 V. Its analogue output passes through a resistor voltage divider to ADC GPIO 34. It responds to several combustible gases and smoke, so its output is a general gas-response value in ADC counts.

8.3 MQ-135 module

The MQ-135 module is powered from 5 V. Its analogue output passes through a separate resistor divider to ADC GPIO 35. It gives a broad air-quality response in ADC counts.

8.4 Sensor interface summary

SensorInterfaceESP32 connectionOutput
AM2301 (DHT21)Digital single-wireGPIO 4°C and % RH
MQ-2Analogue via dividerGPIO 34 (ADC1)Raw ADC counts
MQ-135Analogue via dividerGPIO 35 (ADC1)Raw ADC counts
Ultrasonic sensors (2)TRIG / ECHODedicated GPIO pairsDistance in cm

8.5 MQ sensor conditioning

The MQ modules completed an initial heater burn-in period, and their raw readings are logged as relative gas-response values. They are used as indicators of change in air composition, not as calibrated concentration measurements.

9. Ultrasonic Obstacle Sensing

Two ultrasonic sensors (HC-SR04 type) provide short-range distance estimation around the UGV. Each sensor sends an ultrasonic pulse and measures the echo return time, and the ESP32 converts it to distance.

  • Both HC-SR04 sensors operate on a 5V supply, with individual resistor voltage dividers reducing their ECHO signals to safe 3.3V logic levels before reaching ESP32 GPIO pins 19 and 26.
  • The two sensors are triggered one after the other to avoid cross-interference.
  • Readings are reported in centimetres for nearby obstacles.

10. Camera Subsystem

An ESP32-CAM module with an OV3660 camera provides visual monitoring. It is integrated with the vehicle and streams over Wi-Fi at the same time as the sensor telemetry, giving the operator a live view alongside the environmental data.

Onboard image processing such as obstacle or scene recognition is part of the later Edge-AI stage.

11. Software and Data Acquisition

11.1 Embedded firmware

The ESP32 firmware reads all sensors, formats the values into telemetry records and transmits them over Wi-Fi, while the ESP32-CAM firmware serves the camera feed.

11.2 Telemetry data fields

FieldDescriptionUnit
timestamp_msTime since controller startmilliseconds
sequence_numberRecord counterinteger
temperature_CAM2301 temperature°C
humidity_percentAM2301 relative humidity% RH
mq2_adcRaw MQ-2 readingADC counts
mq135_adcRaw MQ-135 readingADC counts
distance1_cmUltrasonic sensor 1cm
distance2_cmUltrasonic sensor 2cm

11.3 Data logging

Readings are logged as structured CSV records that keep the raw values. The DHT21 is polled within its supported update rate, and its latest valid value is reused between updates in faster telemetry records.

12. Operating Sequence

  1. Power is applied through the protected power-distribution path.
  2. ESP32 controllers initialise their firmware and sensor interfaces.
  3. Environmental sensors provide temperature, humidity and raw analogue readings.
  4. Ultrasonic sensors measure nearby distances.
  5. The ESP32-CAM provides live video over Wi-Fi.
  6. The controller formats the readings into telemetry records.
  7. Sensor data and the camera feed reach the operator device over Wi-Fi.
  8. The operator monitors the vehicle during controlled testing.

This sequence describes operator-monitored operation. Autonomous driving and automatic hazard classification are later stages.

14. Safety and Limitations

Prototype safety boundary: This UGV is an educational and engineering prototype. The ESP32 electronics, MQ sensor modules and battery system are hobby-grade components and are not certified intrinsically safe equipment. The prototype is not deployed in a potentially explosive mine atmosphere and is not a life-safety instrument.

14.1 Technical limitations

  • MQ-2 and MQ-135 respond to many gases and do not replace certified CH4, CO, H2S and O2 instruments.
  • Ultrasonic sensors have limited range and are affected by target angle and surface type.
  • Wi-Fi range inside tunnels is limited, which is the reason for developing the LoRa link.
  • Edge-AI, SLAM and autonomous navigation are later stages of the project.

14.2 Safety functions in the design

  • Independent emergency-stop circuit that cuts motor-drive power.
  • Communication-loss watchdog that stops motion when valid commands stop arriving.
  • Defined safe state on controller reset, sensor fault or low battery.
  • Fuse and battery protection with secured electrical enclosures.

16. Conclusion

The project has reached an integrated prototype stage. The four-wheel UGV platform is built, the environmental and ultrasonic sensors are working, and the ESP32-CAM is integrated. Wi-Fi carries the sensor telemetry and live camera feed together.

The LoRa SX1278 link is the active development item. The next phase completes LoRa telemetry, verifies motor control and the emergency stop, and brings the subsystems together on the moving vehicle. Edge-AI, autonomous navigation and mine deployment follow as later stages.
